response.root_cause: Container exceeded its 256Mi memory limit due to a memory leak in the application, triggering a cgroup OOM kill.

evidence.finding: termination_reason: OOMKilled, exit_code: 137, restart_count: 7, container terminated at 2026-08-29 22:42:54+00:00 after running for ~3 minutes
Memory limit configured at 256Mi; memory request at 128Mi

Previous container logs show continuous memory growth: allocated_mb and rss_mb both increasing linearly from ~48MB/122MB at 22:42:15 to 200MB/273MB at 22:42:53, indicating a memory leak. No shutdown message or exception at termination—consistent with abrupt OOM kill.
Memory utilization peaked at 97.3% of limit at 2026-08-29T22:25:00+00:00 and 78.2% at 2026-08-29T22:42:00+00:00 (just before termination at 22:42:54), showing sustained high utilization
Pod is currently Running with restart_count: 7, indicating repeated OOM kills
Events show 57 BackOff warnings for failed container restarts; no OOMKilled event (expected per runbook—cgroup OOM kills produce no Kubernetes event). No liveness probe failure events detected.

runbook_references: reason: OOMKilled is the decisive field. Check it in lastState.terminated for the container that restarted
If reason is OOMKilled, the container exceeded its memory limit. This is sufficient to confirm the root cause on its own
An OOM kill is abrupt: expect no shutdown message and no stack trace
a cgroup OOM kill produces no event naming OOMKilled. Absence of an OOM event is expected and is not evidence against an OOM diagnosis
recommended_next_steps: Analyze the application code for memory leaks, particularly in the leak_progress event logging path shown in the logs
Determine whether the memory growth is legitimate (working set) or pathological (leak). The linear growth pattern suggests a leak rather than normal operation.
If a leak is confirmed, fix the application. If the working set is legitimately large, raise the memory limit after confirming steady-state usage.
Monitor memory metrics after any fix to verify the leak is resolved and restarts cease
verification_commands: kubectl get events -n incident-demo --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | grep aiops-agentcore-workload
